 127.2  COUNCIL INITIATIVE

  Mayor Butts:

  Initiative by Mayor James T. Butts, Jr., recommending the introduction of an
  Ordinance amending Chapter 8 (Business, Trades, and Professions) of the
  Inglewood Municipal Code to add a new Article 9 (Housing Protection Initiative)
  for the regulation of rent increases and just cause evictions for certain covered
  residential rental units.

  Mayor Butts commented that the City is experiencing an unprecedented economic
  prosperity with much more to come. He stated that the City is at a crossroads. He
  further commented that more Inglewood residents are gainfully employed now
  than any time in city’s history. He stated that although the city’s unemployment
  rate has decreased from 17% to 5.2% in less than 8 years, there are still long term
  residents that are vulnerable, and at risk of sudden displacement without some
  form of economic protection. He commented that this community cannot be the
  city in which prosperity for some comes entirely at the expense of others.
  Mayor Butts stated that he believes government does not have the right to
  arbitrarily decide how private persons operate a business or price their product.
  He commented, however, that he believes that there are instances in which
  government does set standards for the public safety, and welfare. He explained
  that the government requires air bags be built into cars, and fire sprinkler systems
  to be built into buildings, which increases their cost.
  He stated that providing housing is different from selling appliances, clothing,
  office supplies, or jewelry. He also stated people will purchase these items when
  they can afford them, or do without them until they can. He reiterated that
  housing is different. He stated that the demand for housing far exceeds supply.
  He commented that the sudden displacement of renters can destroy the fabric of a
  family’s life. He also stated that providing housing is a complex endeavor
  because the owners must maintain the property, mediate disputes between tenants,

  4
 June 11, 2019

  collect the rent that is sometimes not paid on time, and to attempt to make a fair
  return on what in the end is a business.
  Mayor Butts stated that the City Council has to protect their residents, but must
  also be fair to the owners that provide and maintain the most necessary, and
  precious physical assets in in the community, which is affordable housing. Mayor
  Butts stated that the City Council is not going to forestall economic opportunity in
  order to stay stagnant. He commented that part of providing for this community
  means developing a healthy business tax base, and the City Council wants
  businesses in the city which includes real estate and property management.
  Mayor Butts commented that because of this, everyone has to give a little so that
  in return the residents and investors could all share in the abundance that is
  coming to the City of Inglewood. Mayor Butts made the following motions based
  upon the input that the City Council has received from the community and to
  clean up some things that were not included in the final ordinance. It was moved
  by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City Council
  does hereby amend the Ordinance as follows:
  1. Exclude properties located at 435 W. Regent and 621 E. 99th Street, as the
  owner has previously entered into an agreement with the City.
  2. Allow rental increases up to 5% per year (or the CPI whichever is greater)
  with no relocation allowance.
  3. Allow up to 8% rent increase per annum for up to 2 consecutive years to
  amortize repairs in excess of $10,000. Estimate documentation to be presented to
  the Housing Commission. The inspection will be conducted by the Building
  Department or a contractor of the City’s choice to verify the estimated scope of
  work. The increase will be approved only upon inspection and verification of
  completed work by Building Department personnel and a vote of the Housing
  Commission.
  4. The City will establish an online application process for apartment owners to
  apply for an up to 8% increase exemption to the 5% or CPI cap on rent increases.
  5. Units renting for less than 80% of the average rent for a similar unit
  configuration according to RENTCafe shall be allowed up to an 8% increase in a
  12-month period, with no relocation allowance required, until they reach 81% of
  the aforementioned average market value according to RENTCafe.
  6. Any landlord that offers a relocation allowance to any tenant for a voluntary
  relocation shall be bound by the minimum allowances established in this
  ordinance. The landlord at their discretion may offer more than the established
  relocation minimums.
  7. Relocation will be paid to any tenant removed through No-Fault Eviction if
  that tenant has been a resident for 2 years or more.
  8. The rental increase application panel shall consist of members of the Housing
  Commission appointed by the City Council. The panel shall consist of at least
  two renters and two apartment owners.
  Council Member Morales:
  Council Member Morales stated that he supports the motions made by Mayor
  Butts. He also made a friendly motion to include when it comes to creating a
  Housing Board Commission for owners to request an increase up to 8%, that the
  Board be made up of 2 renters, 2 owners, and a homeowner that are citizens of
  Inglewood, and selected by District.

  5
 June 11, 2019

  Council Member Dotson:
  Council Member Dotson stated that he would like to applaud Mayor Butts, and
  the rest of the City Council for their hard work regarding this matter. He stated
  that this Ordinance needed to be done, in order to protect the tenants. He also
  stated that this Moratorium will make most of the residents happy, but the City
  Council won’t be able to please everyone. He stated there will need to be some
  give and take, but hopefully it pleases most of the people.
  Council Member Padilla:
  Council Member Padilla commented he appreciates everyone who came out to the
  City Council meeting today (Tenants and Owners). He expressed how he shared
  with his family how this issue really wears on you, because you realize it will
  impact so many.  He also stated that when folks come out to the Council
  meetings to express their concerns, the City Council is listening to their stories
  about being displaced or homeless. He assured property owners that the City
  Council is also working to help them keep their investments, and their legacy, so
  that they can continue to have their investments and legacy for their families.
  Council Member Padilla stated that the City Council had to find a medium, and he
  hopes people will embrace the Rent Stabilization Ordinance. He thanked the
  Mayor for his leadership, wisdom and for reaching out to the others who helped
  the City Council put this Moratorium together. Lastly, he thanked everyone again
  for coming out.
  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Franklin.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 19-11 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA ADDING A NEW ARTICLE 9 “HOUSING
  PROTECTION INITIATIVE” TO CHAPTER 8 OF THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO REGULATE RENT
  INCREASES AND JUST CAUSE EVICTIONS FOR CERTAIN
  COVERED RESIDENTIAL RENTAL UNITS

  was introduced as amended by Mayor Butts.

  City Attorney Ken Campos:

  City Council to bring back an urgency ordinance to cover the lapse in time until
  an ordinance becomes effective.
  Mayor Butts affirmed.
  City Attorney Ken Campos also asked for a write-up of the amendments made to
  the Ordinance.
  Mayor Butts commented he will be sure to get the amendments to the City
  Attorney and City Clerk.
